name: ITAR classification helper for small exporters
demand: The clearest ITAR-specific population proxy is roughly 14,500 DDTC registrants in FY2023, cited in a 2024 State Department rule; it is not a current count of small-business buyers. (https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2024-29032.pdf?1733519716=) The Census Bureau reported 270,001 identified U.S. exporters in 2024, including 262,281 small and medium exporters and 62,849 small and medium manufacturing exporters; these are broad ceilings, not ITAR-qualified market counts. The data was released December 11, 2025. (https://www.census.gov/foreign-trade/Press-Release/edb/2024prelimprofile.pdf) Search volume, installs, active users, and the small-business share of DDTC registrants: unverified.
prices: ITAR Screen lists $99/month, $249/month, and $499/month plans. (https://www.itarscreen.com/pricing) ECCN.dev lists a free reference and $49/month Solo and $149/month Team plans. (https://eccn.dev/pricing) ExChek offers its engine free, with $149/month Starter and $499/month Professional plans. (https://exchek.us/) ECCN.help includes five workflow classifications; price for additional classifications is unverified. (https://eccn.help/pricing.php) BIS provides free CCL and Order of Review tools and a route to request an official classification. (https://www.bis.gov/licensing/classify-your-item)

revenue_proof.claim: Unverified: the public ITAR Screen pricing page shows asking prices, not customer payments, recognized revenue, or paid-customer counts.

copy_speed: The cheap-check claim of no recent launches is contradicted by ExChek’s exact April 28, 2026 launch of an agent-oriented export compliance engine covering ECCN classification, screening, licensing, and records. (https://exchek.us/press/) BITE Data says it launched an agentic export-control and classification tool “this month” in a LinkedIn post; the exact post date is unverified. (https://www.linkedin.com/company/bitedata) Exporra’s site states a June 2026 launch but invites users to request early access, so availability is unverified. (https://www.exporra.com/) ECCN.io announced public access for January 2026, outside the six-month window, but its page still says “pre-register”; actual availability is unverified. (https://eccn.io/) One exact in-window launch is verified; the two-launch kill threshold is not established from exact dates.
platform_risk: A product distributed mainly as an AI-agent plugin would depend on changing agent platforms; ExChek currently advertises hosted MCP and REST access while saying its plugin is retiring. (https://exchek.us/) A standalone web workflow or API would reduce that dependency. There is also a material data-hosting issue: DDTC says cloud storage avoids constituting an ITAR export only under conditions including U.S.-based servers, U.S.-person-only administration, and customer-controlled access. A UK-based founder handling plaintext controlled data could create a conflict; that is an architecture risk to confirm with export-control counsel, not a legal conclusion. (https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/ddtc_public?id=ddtc_public_portal_faq_detail&sysparm_article=KB0010950)
defensible_asset: A maintained, versioned rules engine could meet the stated moat requirement, but the corpus is mainly based on public regulations and official lists, and BIS already supplies free self-classification tools. ITAR Screen and ExChek publicly offer similar classification and record workflows. (https://www.bis.gov/licensing/classify-your-item) (https://www.itarscreen.com/) (https://exchek.us/) Customer histories could create some switching friction, but ECCN.dev says customers can export their files, while ITAR Screen says customer data is isolated and not used to train models without consent; those practices weaken a shared-data or network-effect moat. (https://eccn.dev/pricing) (https://www.itarscreen.com/terms) The proposed moat is therefore a build requirement, not yet an established durable advantage.
build_effort: High. A credible product needs maintained rule versions, citations, reproducible records, careful treatment of ambiguous cases, and a secure way to handle product information. BIS says self-classification requires technical understanding and offers an official classification-request route. (https://www.bis.gov/licensing/classify-your-item) ITAR Screen labels its output preliminary and recommends qualified counsel; its terms also describe ten-year record retention. (https://www.itarscreen.com/terms) For a UK-based operator, local-first processing or a design that prevents founder access to controlled technical data appears necessary to investigate, given DDTC’s cloud conditions. (https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/ddtc_public?id=ddtc_public_portal_faq_detail&sysparm_article=KB0010950)
channel: Use inbound SEO pages for classification questions, listings in software and AI-agent marketplaces, self-serve integrations/API directories, and opt-in referrals through export-compliance consultants. Use paid search only after checking applicable advertising, privacy, and platform rules in the UK and target market. No cold email, SMS, DMs, or calls.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified; there is no operating evidence that this product can stay within 5 hours per week. Human review for ambiguous classifications, regulatory changes, and customer escalations may exceed that limit.
automation_reason: Estimate for a mature, steady-state product, not an observed operating result: agents could handle routine rule-change monitoring and draft updates, classification intake, report generation, billing/admin, and first-line support. Expert validation of rule changes and ambiguous cases, security decisions, and channel partnerships still require human oversight. Existing tools explicitly frame classification as preliminary or human-approved, so the proposed automation share and founder-hours limit remain unverified. (https://www.itarscreen.com/terms) (https://exchek.us/)
moat_assessment: Weak as currently evidenced. A maintained rules engine qualifies in principle, but public source material and close, low-priced or free competitors make the mapping easy to copy. History-based switching costs are possible but weakened by exportable customer records; no network effect is evident. The lead does not yet demonstrate that its rules corpus or reviewed edge cases would be materially better than existing products. (https://www.bis.gov/licensing/classify-your-item) (https://www.itarscreen.com/pricing) (https://eccn.dev/pricing) (https://exchek.us/)
desk_test: One workday, no cold outreach: use Google Ads Keyword Planner to check current search volume and CPC for exact-intent phrases such as “ITAR classification software” and “USML classification”; then run several synthetic, publicly documented product descriptions through BIS’s free tools, ITAR Screen’s free classifications, and ExChek. Record mismatches, citations, and where each workflow requires human review. If the gaps look material, put up a no-code page with a clear price and opt-in waitlist through an inbound channel. Search demand and willingness to pay remain unverified by this test. (https://www.bis.gov/licensing/classify-your-item) (https://www.itarscreen.com/) (https://exchek.us/)
red_flags: No verified revenue, paid-customer counts, search demand, or user adoption found; posted prices are not proof of payment. (https://www.itarscreen.com/pricing) The recent competition makes the original “none found” conclusion stale: ExChek has an exact in-window launch, with additional recent or announced competitors whose exact launch status is not verified. (https://exchek.us/press/) (https://www.linkedin.com/company/bitedata) (https://www.exporra.com/) Free official BIS tools and ExChek’s free engine pressure pricing. (https://www.bis.gov/licensing/classify-your-item) (https://exchek.us/) Acceptance of automated classification without expert review is unverified; ITAR Screen calls results preliminary and recommends expert counsel. (https://www.itarscreen.com/terms) UK-based founder access to controlled technical data may complicate cloud operation under DDTC’s stated conditions; validate the architecture with qualified counsel before handling such data. (https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/ddtc_public?id=ddtc_public_portal_faq_detail&sysparm_article=KB0010950)
